title: O God of Mercy! Hear My Call
description: O God of Mercy! Hear My Call in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 51, part 5, headed “Repentance and faith in the blood of Christ”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God of mer-cy! hear my call, My loads of guilt re-move; Break down this sep-a-rat-ing wall That bars me from thy love.

lines: O God of mercy! hear my call,
That bars me from thy love.
Give me the presence of thy grace,
And make thy praise my song.
No blood of goats, nor heifers slain,
The death of Christ shall still remain
A soul opprest with sin's desert,
A humble groan, a broken heart

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
